'''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} located in {{ill|Jōyō, Kyoto|en|Jōyō, Kyoto|qid=Q817276|lt=Joyo, Kyoto}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|en|Kyoto Prefecture|qid=Q120730|lt=Kyoto Prefecture}}, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun is designated as a National Historic Site, and its burial goods are designated as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}}.
== Overview ==
Shibagahara Kofun was constructed on a hill in the northern part of Joyo City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurumazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11369464}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Showa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park.
While originally a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks ste11ed construction and exterior stone covering (fukiishi){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} but is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly unique<ref name="Joyo City Tourism Association"/>.
The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century during the early {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}}<ref name="Joyo City Tourism Association">[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).</ref>. It is considered one of the most prominent Kofuns of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|en|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|qid=Q11540994|lt=Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}.
The site was designated a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1)<ref name="National Historic Site"/> and its grave goods were designated National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} in 1990 (Heisei 2)<ref name="National Historic Site"/>.
== Excavation History ==
* '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education<ref name="National Historic Site"/>.
* '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6<ref name="National Historic Site"/>.
* '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods designated as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} on June 29<ref name="National Historic Site"/>.
* '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded Historic Site of historic site boundaries<ref name="National Historic Site"/>.

== burial goods ==
[[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Bronze Mirror with Four Beasts}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]]
[[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze Bracelet}}]]
Major burial goods recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}:
* '''Bronze mirror with four beasts''' - 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror).
* '''Bronze bracelets''' - 2 pieces (matching set).
* '''Jade magatama beads''' - 8 pieces.
* '''Jasper tubular beads''' - 187 pieces.
* '''Glass small beads''' - 1,276 pieces.
* '''Yariganna chisel''' - 1 piece.
Additionally, shards of Shōnai-style pottery, including double-rimmed jars and tall-stemmed bowls, were found on the Kofun surface as offerings{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan)<ref name="Joyo City Tourism Association"/>.

== Historic Site ==
=== Important Cultural Property (National Designation) ===
* '''burial goods Excavated from Shibagahara Kofun, Kyoto Prefecture''' - Designated June 29, 1990<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|10078|burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun}}</ref>.
=== National Historic Site ===
* '''Shibagahara Kofun''' - Designated September 6, 1989, with expanded boundaries on January 24, 2012<ref name="National Historic Site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}}</ref>.
== Related Facilities ==
* '''Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan)''' (Terada Imahoricho, Joyo City) - Houses and exhibits burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun.
